headline: Why Corporate SaaS Login Walls Kill Soul

left.headline: The Landlord Model (Bloat)
body: Forces an email + password + OTP wall before you even use the tool.
Stores user notes in plaintext Postgres tables waiting to be breached.
Charges $20/mo recurring subscriptions for a glorified scratchpad.
Treats identity like a government DMV form instead of a toy you own.

right.headline: The Cartridge Model (Sovereign)
body: App works 100% locally on millisecond one — zero sign-up gate.
Pay once ($39/yr) -> receive a holographic, collectible **Passport Cartridge**.
One secret unlocks your perks AND derives your encrypted device-sync room.
The server never knows your name, your email, or a single word you dictated.

headline: Four Layers From One Secret
body: Everything in TalkType's Passport flows deterministically from one root secret.

pillars.title: 1. Deterministic Mint
pillars.text: `licenseIdForCheckout()` HMACs the Square checkout ID so webhook + browser polling race safely without duplicate records.

pillars.title: 2. Blind Verification
pillars.text: Server stores only `HMAC(code)` + a 365-day term. Browser holds a signed HS256 JWT (`v:2`) for instant cloud admission.

pillars.title: 3. PBKDF2 -> HKDF Sync
pillars.text: 100,000 rounds of PBKDF2 + HKDF split your secret into a public `roomId` and a private `AES-GCM-256` key. Relay sees only noise.

pillars.title: 4. Collectible Soul
pillars.text: `vaultHash` seeds your procedural moniker (**Mossy Otter**), DiceBear avatar, and 60fps pointer-reactive holofoil skin.

headline: The Cartridge: What's Actually Stored vs. Derived
body: **Right now in the code**: When you buy or redeem a Passport, you get a personal `TT-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` code. The server only stores its SHA-256 HMAC (`codeHash`) plus three idempotent buckets: your 1-year term, your Deepgram Nova-3 bank, and your Gemini restyle budget.

**Shared Promo Words (`supporterPass.js`)**: If you type a shared promo word like `MAESTRO`, the server automatically trades it in for your **own personal `TT-XXXX` code** so everyone who used the promo word doesn't end up in the same sync room!
**Your Identity (`identityUtils.js`)**: Your `vaultHash` deterministically generates your card persona — e.g. **Mossy Otter** (*"mossy otter drifts at midnight"*) + custom holofoil palette.

headline: Zero-Knowledge Sync: Why the Relay Is Blindfolded
body: How do your phone and laptop find each other without an account? **`syncCrypto.js`** runs `PBKDF2 (100,000 iterations, SHA-256)` on your Passport secret (+ optional 4-word phrase), then splits that seed via **HKDF** into two mathematically independent keys:
**1. `softstack:sync:room:v2`** -> Derives the 128-bit `roomId` that the WebSocket/HTTP relay sees.

**2. `softstack:sync:key:v2`** -> Derives the 256-bit `AES-GCM` key that seals every note (`{ iv, ct }`) before it leaves your browser. Walking backward from `roomId` to your code costs 100k PBKDF2 rounds per guess.

headline: Four Cute Words vs. Hex Codes: Where We Are & How to Finish It
body: **Reality check**: Right now, TalkType has **two** word systems: `identityUtils.js` makes your card's poetic subtitle (*"mossy otter drifts at midnight"*), and `syncPhrase.js` generates a 4-word private room phrase (`neon otter drifts quietly`, `40^4 = 2.56M` combos) to fork a shared sync room.
**The gap**: Today, the actual unlock code the server checks is still `TT-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`. You can't type *"neon otter drifts quietly"* into the Redeem box to unlock a new browser yet.

**How to make 4 Cute Words the ACTUAL unlock key**: Map `4 words (+ optional 2-digit number/emoji)` -> `codeHash` on mint (`neon-otter-drifts-82` = ~256M combos). Easy to say out loud, easy to type on a phone, zero hex soup!

headline: "Email Me My Passport" — The 80/20 Missing Link

left.headline: The Only Real Risk Today
body: Because we don't force an email/password database, what happens when someone buys a new iPhone 6 months later or wipes Safari?
If they didn't save their `TT-XXXX` code or keep a second device linked, they have no 'Forgot Password' button.

right.headline: The 'Email Me My Passport' Button
body: Add a `[ ✉️ Email me my Passport ]` button right under the holofoil card.
Sends ONE cute Soft Neo Toybrut HTML email: cream `#fffdf5` card, **Mossy Otter** badge, their 4-word / `TT-XXXX` key, and a giant hot-pink **`[ Unlock My TalkType Passport ]`** magic link.
We never store their email in a database — their own inbox becomes their permanent, searchable vault!

headline: Four Nouns in the Codebase (Why Your Brain Felt Fuzzy)
body: It evolved across 3 eras, so one system currently wears four hats in the code:

items.label: Passport — The user-facing product & holofoil MembershipCard.svelte
Supporter — The server JWT & quota tier (isSupporter, licenseStore.js)
Vault — The SHA-256 identity hash & encrypted cloud backup (vaultHash)
SoftStack Sync — The PBKDF2 + HKDF + AES-GCM live device beam
